purpose: Maribavir is used to treat a viral infection called cytomegalovirus, or CMV, in people who have had an organ or stem cell transplant. It is specifically used when other antiviral treatments have stopped working or the virus has become resistant to them. It helps your body fight off this serious infection so you can recover.
how_it_works: CMV is a virus that can be very dangerous for people with weakened immune systems, like transplant patients. Maribavir works by blocking a specific protein the virus needs to copy itself and spread in your body. By stopping the virus from making more copies of itself, the medication helps reduce the amount of virus in your blood and clear the infection.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include changes in your sense of taste (things may taste different or strange), feeling sick to your stomach (nausea), vomiting, diarrhea, and feeling tired or fatigued. Some people also notice stomach pain or decreased appetite. Tell your doctor or pharmacist if any of these bother you.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are taking ganciclovir or valganciclovir, because maribavir can block how those medicines work and they should not be used together. It is important to let your healthcare team know all the medications, vitamins, and supplements you take, as maribavir can interact with many drugs. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medication. Do not stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 400 mg (two 200 mg tablets) taken by mouth twice a day, with or without food. Your doctor will tell you exactly how long to take it, but treatment is typically for 8 weeks. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep steady levels of the medicine in your body.
